liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Never Trust A Woman** (2 reviews): Never Trust A Woman is likened to Brent's You Ain't Woman Enough; Jerry opens it up but it has limited room; Never Trust A Woman is called one of the better tunes Brent played with the Dead [16][19]
- **Passenger** (2 reviews): Passenger knocked the reviewer's socks off, and he danced even when ushers tried to make him sit; Passenger is described as a liftoff, starting an excellent stretch of the first set [17][18]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Lost Sailor is laid back and slick, then falls into a jammed Saint of Circumstance [12]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Franklin's Tower is played at the fastest tempo the reviewer has ever heard, perhaps not ideal for the song [16]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Not Fade Away coming out of Space is groovy [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd81-12-02 s1t01 Bertha**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd81-12-02 s1t02 Greatest Story Ever Told**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd81-12-02 s1t03 Peggy O**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd81-12-02 s1t04 Mama Tried**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd81-12-02 s1t05 Mexicali Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd81-12-02 s1t06 Brown Eyed Women**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd81-12-02 s1t07 Passenger**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **gd81-12-02 s1t08 Never Trust A Woman**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-12-02.144277.fob.senn421.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 26 songs; 166 min [1]. Said about its sound: The first few notes of Bertha are missing from the recording [1]
- **gd1981-12-02.158823.mtx.seamons.ht147.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 168 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience source lacks the end of Terrapin Station through the start of Space; Soundboard source is missing Stella Blue through the end of the show, plus a brief cut in Terrapin Station [3]
- **gd1981-12-02.sbd.miller.108842.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 167 min; rated 3.33/5 by 6 [4]
- **gd1981-12-02.145662.s1.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 12 songs; 75 min [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer likens this show's blazing energy to the Indianapolis show three nights later, in the hard-driving early-'80s period [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-12-02.144277.fob.senn421.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Frank Streeter's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M (TDK MA-C90) [1]. Also: Most of Drums (9:16 total) comes from the Miller soundboard source shnid 108842; no other patches exist [1]
- **gd1981-12-02.158823.mtx.seamons.ht147.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut w/EQ > Soundtrack Pro > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging)… [3]. Also: Newer soundboard had heavy tape distortion late in Passenger, so the older soundboard source patched it [3]
- **gd1981-12-02.sbd.miller.108842.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [4]. Also: Joe B. Jones helped pitch-correct the patch source used in this soundboard [4]
- **gd1981-12-02.145662.s1.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXL-II-C90) [6]. Also: Soundboard traces from cassette master to reel to DAT, with all transfers and mastering by Charlie Miller; The first 5:31 of Never Trust A Woman is supplied from the shnid 108842 source [6]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by John Rottet Grateful Dead: [1981-12-02 Assembly Hall, U. of Illinois, Champaign, IL, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1981-12-02-assembly-hall-u-of-illinois-champaign-il-usa/) [21]
- Poster by urbanafreelibrary.org: [Grateful Dead Descend on Assembly Hall | Urbana Free Library](https://urbanafreelibrary.org/local-history/blog/grateful-dead-descend-assembly-hall) [22]
